subject: ordering
subject_note: The commit point. This is a journey document, not a single-service one, so the graph is anchored at the deployable where the order is created, shipped and cancelled. The adapter anchors the graph here and records the subject.
source: Transcribed from PHASE-3-6-RECONCILE-RULE-SELECT-OBSERVE.md, Phase 3, the reconciliation table. Not re-derived — this is the same run's own rulings, moved from a markdown table into the shape the adapter reads.

stages.name: Customer chooses what to buy
stages.description: The customer browses the catalogue. Served by the catalogue read surface.

stages.name: Customer holds items until ready
stages.description: Items are held in a basket that can be read, updated and emptied.

stages.name: Business acknowledges the order
stages.description: An order-submitted announcement is picked up by the web application.

stages.name: Short window to change their mind
stages.description: A background worker runs the grace period, then confirms it has elapsed.

stages.name: Check the goods are available
stages.description: Stock is checked and answered as confirmed or rejected — two distinct announcements.

stages.name: Business takes the money
stages.description: A payment service exists and it charges nobody — it decides its outcome by reading a configuration setting, so no gateway is contacted. Present in structure, hollow in function.

stages.name: Confirm the order is going ahead
stages.description: Stock is decremented, and the web application and subscribed partners are told.

stages.name: Pick and ship the goods
stages.description: A ship endpoint exists and works, and nothing in this system calls it. What cannot be measured is the physical fulfilment, not the transition.

stages.name: Customer is told it shipped
stages.description: An order-shipped announcement reaches the web application and partners.

stages.name: Tell partners what happened
stages.description: Dispatch to subscribed third parties. Subscription management is a separate surface.

stages.name: Handle cancellation or failure
stages.condition: the order is cancelled, payment fails, or stock is rejected
stages.description: Three distinct branches — cancellation, payment failure, stock rejection.
